summary: This document releases IANA-assigned port numbers for NETCONF-related services that have not been used in production networks. Those ports can then be reused.

plainLanguage.summary: Three port numbers assigned to NETCONF services were not in use in production networks. This RFC releases those numbers while keeping the service names in the registry.

subtitle: IANA releases three unused port numbers assigned to NETCONF services.

tldr.problem: Ports 831, 832, and 833 remained assigned to NETCONF-related services that were not deployed and whose RFCs were Historic.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC removes the port assignments but retains the service names in the registry.
tldr.outcome: The port numbers are available for other uses; existing configurations using the service names should be reassessed.

today: RFC 9900 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Unused NETCONF Port Assignments
sections.content:
The IANA registry listed ports for several NETCONF services, including 830 for NETCONF over SSH, 831 for NETCONF over BEEP, and 832 for NETCONF over SOAP. The document also lists 833 for NETCONF over SOAP over BEEP.

Ports 831, 832 and 833 were assigned to protocols that were not deployed; the relevant RFCs had been marked Historic. RFC 9900 de-assigns the port numbers.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC identifies ports 831, 832, and 833 as assignments for services that were not deployed. It releases those numbers from the registry.

sections.title: What Changes in the Registry
sections.content:
The registry entries for NETCONF over BEEP at 831 and NETCONF over SOAP services at 832 and 833 no longer contain port assignments. Notes identify the former assignments and say RFC 9900 released them.

The service names are not de-assigned. Following RFC 6335, only the port numbers are released for later use.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry keeps the service names but removes their port numbers. The numbers can then be assigned for another use.

sections.title: Operational and Security Notes
sections.content:
The RFC reports no known implementations or deployments relying on the released port numbers. Any existing configurations associating the numbers with netconf-beep or netconfsoaphttp need to be reassessed.

This document does not describe a protocol and introduces no new security vulnerability.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC knows of no deployed implementation that depends on the released numbers. Any configuration that still uses them should be checked.

references.text: Cotton, M., Eggert, L., Touch, J., Westerlund, M., and S. Cheshire, "Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) Procedures for the Management of the Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry", BCP 165, RFC 6335, August 2011.
Goddard, T., "Using NETCONF over the Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP)", RFC 4743, December 2006.
Lear, E. and K. Crozier, "Using the NETCONF Protocol over the Blocks Extensible Exchange Protocol (BEEP)", RFC 4744, December 2006.
